displacement._schema: v1.27 (Brief 7 Phase 1). Migrated off the retired global amplitude_m 0.4 to per-layer metres keyed by this pre-8K recipe's three layers (Snow/Rock/Grass). Legacy EVALUATION world; migrated only so the shared displacement_spec/_validate_displacement schema bump does not refuse a committed recipe. prove_gates.py exercises this recipe's displacement_spec.

rock_scatter._comment: SHARED PHYSICAL FACT (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 19). Read by BOTH the Pass 2 landscape material's scree sub-surface mask AND Pass 3's talus mesh scatter. Defined once here; neither consumer may keep its own copy. These are properties of rock, not style knobs.

canopy._comment: SHARED PHYSICAL FACT (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 19), sibling to rock_scatter. The canopy radius is a MEASURED property of the tree, not a style knob, and any consumer that clusters under trees reads it from here. Currently read by rock_scatter.py via placement_priors.canopy_occupancy for Pass 5 ground clutter.
canopy._source: Free/_measured/fir_tree_01.json -> object fir_tree_01_c_LOD0, dims_xyz [6.305939, 5.96624, 14.520583] m. radius_m is the mean horizontal half-extent: (6.305939 + 5.96624) / 4 = 3.068 m. This is the mesh PLACED as Conifer (foliage.species[].mesh ends fir_tree_01_c_LOD0), not the higher-poly _a or _b variants, which measure 6.534 x 6.427 and 5.613 x 6.057.

palette._verified_policy: Every entry is verified=false. Promotion requires a spawn and a render, in the pass that places the asset. This file cannot assert true.

tier_gate.rule: A blob-shaped rock asset is admitted only if its measured density falls inside the reference group's observed range. Planar and spanning assets are NOT gated by this metric — see the limits in scripts/palette_evidence.py.

surface_rulings.criteria: coherence with Rock051 at the talus boundary; tiling at ground AND 2 km; displacement quality, since scree is where displacement reads most

rejected.disqualifier: CONTENT, not statistics: it is MOSS-COVERED VEGETATED BEDROCK, bright green, not fractured stone. Scree is by definition unvegetated — talus is actively moving, which is exactly why vegetation cannot establish on it. A mossy scree field is a geological error.
rejected.why_the_numbers_said_otherwise: Every numeric coherence metric FAVOURED Rock063: RGB distance from Rock051 0.197 vs Rock026's 0.338, and luminance ratio 0.91x vs 1.45x. Those metrics cannot distinguish 'similar brown rock' from 'green moss at similar luminance' — the low blue channel (0.192) that reads as warm-rust in numbers is chlorophyll. The disqualifier was found by LOOKING at the contact sheet, and by nothing else.
rejected.secondary: Also 4096x2048, a 2:1 aspect that the builder's single scalar UV divisor would stretch 2:1.

winner_weaknesses_recorded_not_hidden: Displacement detail is WEAK: laplacian std 0.00200 against Rock051's 0.00623 (3.1x less), and its range is compressed to 0.242..0.909 rather than full. This is the criterion that matters most for scree.

Low-frequency energy is 0.1364, 2.07x Rock051's 0.0659 — the most visible-tiling candidate of the three at the 2 km verification scale. The macro-variation layer (Pass 2c) is what must break it up, and this is the surface that will test it.

Luminance is 1.45x Rock051. Judged ACCEPTABLE rather than ignored: fresh rockfall exposes unweathered interior with no lichen, so scree genuinely IS lighter than the weathered cliff above it. This one is physically right, not merely tolerated.
surface_rulings.mitigation_already_in_the_design: R2's PASS 2 UPGRADE requires the HeightLerp transition contrast to be PER LAYER PAIR, derived from each surface's measured displacement range. Rock026's weak, compressed height map is exactly the case that requirement exists for; one global contrast constant would render this pair nearly unblended.
surface_rulings.honest_verdict: Rock026 is the better of two, not a good scree surface. It is the only candidate of the right MATERIAL CLASS. A dedicated scree/talus scan would beat it and is a BACKLOG intake item.

excluded.group: Rock063 — rejected as the scree surface
excluded.reason: Moss-covered vegetated bedrock, not fractured stone. See surface_rulings.scree_surface. Every numeric metric favoured it; the contact sheet disqualified it in one look.
excluded.disposition: Not imported. Genuinely useful LATER for wet shaded bedrock near drainage, where moss is correct — that is a different role, and it would need its 2:1 aspect handled.

excluded.group: DragonCave — all rock and stone meshes
excluded.reason: MEASURED below the region's quality tier and NOT MARGINALLY. Median 14.5 tri/m2 for SM_LargeRock* (n=7) and 21.9 for SM_CaveRock* (n=4), against 299.5 for the KiteDemo rock reference group (n=12). The ranges do not overlap at all: the KiteDemo minimum is 105.8 and the DragonCave maximum is 23.9, so no DragonCave rock is as dense as the sparsest KiteDemo rock. This is an exclusion by measurement, not by taste.
excluded.disposition: Keep for cave/dungeon interiors, where the lighting is close and the silhouette carries the read. Catalogue only; not alpine inventory.
